entities.summary: Ambrogio Calepino, a renowned Italian lexicographer, played a pivotal role in shaping the linguistic landscape of the Renaissance. Born in unknown circumstances, Calepino dedicated his life to compiling and editing Latin texts, which had a profound impact on the development of the Italian language. His most notable work, the 'Lexicon', a comprehensive dictionary of Latin words, became a cornerstone of linguistic study for centuries. Calepino's contributions also influenced the emergence of the Italian language as a distinct literary and cultural force. The 'Lexicon' remained a vital resource for scholars and linguists until the 18th century, a testament to Calepino's enduring legacy. As a key figure in the transmission of classical knowledge, Calepino's work continues to be studied and appreciated by scholars today, offering valuable insights into the evolution of language and culture in Renaissance Italy.
